name: Anonymous Bot
description: A Slack app. Someone types a command and the message shows up in an allowed channel without a name. Plans are free, $50, or $100 a month. Founder Fernando Falci. Running since 2020.

mentions.evidence: MRR $891. 11 subscriptions. Last 30 days $791. Last 12 months $12,540. All-time $51,083. Last-30-day margin 99% claimed. Listed for sale at $100,000 (10.5x). Revenue synced 4 November 2026 ~04:23 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: One Slack command a workplace actually uses, priced per workspace.

whyItPrints: One command, and it has been on since 2020. The seller says nothing was spent on marketing and about $10 on servers. The asking price is a high multiple.
whyThisMatters:
Anonymous Bot posts into Slack without attaching a name. The command is short. Channels can be limited. Free, fifty a month, or a hundred a month. Fernando Falci has run it since 2020.

Eleven Stripe subscriptions, a bit under nine hundred a month. The last year is about twelve thousand, and the all-time total is about fifty thousand, so the early years were not empty and the recent pace is not a spike. Margin is claimed at ninety-nine percent. He says marketing spend was zero and servers cost about ten dollars. The asking price is a hundred thousand, more than ten times the monthly line. That multiple is the odd part. The product itself is a small command that people leave installed.

You pay so a message can land in the channel without a name on it.

Allowed channels are the limit. Fernando Falci is the founder. Zero marketing spend and about ten dollars of servers are his costs. Ten and a half times is the asking multiple.
